newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-COACH URGES SMALL TO BEFRIEND BOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-COACH URGES SMALL TO BEFRIEND BOKS.

text.p: Springbok rugby union coach Andre Markgraaff urged tempestuous winger James Small on Saturday to bury the hatchet with his teammates so he could get back into the national side.
"James Small's position is not in my hands, it's in James Small's hands," Markgraaff, who dropped Small for last month's tests against the All Blacks, said in a television interview.
"He's a brilliant player, I'd love to have him in the team. He must just sort out his problems with his fellow-players.
"If he can do that, we'll pick him, but it depends on James Small," the coach said.
According to newspaper reports, Small was not considered for the All Blacks series because he had fallen out with several other members of the Springbok side.
He was reported to have sworn at some of them during one test and to have come close to blows with fellow-winger Pieter Hendricks in the changerooms.
Small, with 31 caps, is one of the most experienced of the current batch of Springboks.

"If he is 50 percent better than the next best wing in South Africa, but if his influence on the team reduces the performance of the team by 60 percent, then you have to ask yourself if you can pick him," Markgraaff said.
South Africa begin a tour to Argentina, France and Wales in November.
